docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-420-Findings:
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-421-- **All cos²-scaled configs are stable**, including A_h=5e5 (50× the
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-422-  Phase-4 value).  The Arctic high-lat blow-up that killed uniform 2e5
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-423-  is **demonstrably fixed**.
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-424-- **The 2Δy zonal-jet mode is essentially gone** at A_h_global ≥ 1e5
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-425-  (see `results/ocean/cos2lat_sweep/partial_u_comparison.png`).  Basin
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-426-  interior u is near-zero everywhere except at the equator.
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-427-- **Diminishing returns 2e5 → 5e5**: only 0.06 m/s improvement in p95;
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md:428:  equator zonal-mean drops 0.53 → 0.45.
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-429-- **Equatorial residual saturates at ~0.4-0.5 m/s** — this is the
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-430-  resolution-limited floor.  ~0.4 cells per equatorial Rossby radius
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-431-  at 5° means we can't represent equatorial wave structure properly,
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-432-  and the model dumps that energy into 2Δy stripes that no closure
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-433-  can fully eliminate.  Only finer equatorial resolution does.
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-434-
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-435-**Recommended production setting: cos²(lat) + A_h_global = 2e5.**
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-436-Reasoning: 5e5 is marginally cleaner numerically but starts damping
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-437-mid-latitude gyres/boundary currents.  2e5 corresponds to the MOM6
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-438-grid-Reynolds-rule scaling from their 1° default (A_h~1e4 × Δx²
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-439-ratio 25 ≈ 2.5e5).  Leaves headroom for western boundary currents to
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-440-organize while still suppressing the 2Δy mode 4× from the current
docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-441-default.

./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-420-Findings:
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-421-- **All cos²-scaled configs are stable**, including A_h=5e5 (50× the
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-422-  Phase-4 value).  The Arctic high-lat blow-up that killed uniform 2e5
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-423-  is **demonstrably fixed**.
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-424-- **The 2Δy zonal-jet mode is essentially gone** at A_h_global ≥ 1e5
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-425-  (see `results/ocean/cos2lat_sweep/partial_u_comparison.png`).  Basin
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-426-  interior u is near-zero everywhere except at the equator.
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-427-- **Diminishing returns 2e5 → 5e5**: only 0.06 m/s improvement in p95;
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md:428:  equator zonal-mean drops 0.53 → 0.45.
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-429-- **Equatorial residual saturates at ~0.4-0.5 m/s** — this is the
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-430-  resolution-limited floor.  ~0.4 cells per equatorial Rossby radius
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-431-  at 5° means we can't represent equatorial wave structure properly,
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-432-  and the model dumps that energy into 2Δy stripes that no closure
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-433-  can fully eliminate.  Only finer equatorial resolution does.
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-434-
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-435-**Recommended production setting: cos²(lat) + A_h_global = 2e5.**

./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-437-mid-latitude gyres/boundary currents.  2e5 corresponds to the MOM6
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-438-grid-Reynolds-rule scaling from their 1° default (A_h~1e4 × Δx²
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-439-ratio 25 ≈ 2.5e5).  Leaves headroom for western boundary currents to
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-440-organize while still suppressing the 2Δy mode 4× from the current
./docs/ocean/experiments/realistic_geometry_phase4_results.md-441-default.

docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-250-
docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-251-1. **Accept O(dx) artifacts**: At C48+, artifacts are < 0.4 m/s and may be acceptable for coupled ESM. The baseline model at C36 shows L2=0.013 (5-day TC2, stable), max|v|=1.4 m/s, mass drift < 1e-7. This is competitive with published cubed-sphere solvers.
docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-252-
docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-253-2. **Higher-order halo exchange** (DONE, iteration 9): Upgraded pad_halo halo=1 from 2-point linear to 3-point quadratic Lagrange. Provides ~3% reduction in max |v| edge artifacts. Limited improvement because for smooth geostrophic fields, B''' ≈ B''/h, so the O(h³→h²) gradient error improvement is only O(h) ≈ 1/36 at C36. Further upgrades (5-point, duo-grid) would give diminishing returns for the same reason.
docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-254-
docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-255-3. **Switch to FV3's normal D-grid layout** (GFDL convention): Each velocity component at its NORMAL face (u_ξ at ξ-face, u_η at η-face). This enables simple 2-point gradients WITHOUT the Cartesian matrix — eliminating the error source entirely. Requires rewriting ALL cubed-sphere operators, mass transport, halo exchange, and initial conditions. Multi-month effort.

docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-275-**Why only ~3% improvement**: For a smooth geostrophic field (TC2), B''' ≈ B''/h. This means the O(h³→h²) gradient error improvement from quadratic→cubic is only O(h) ≈ 1/n, which at C36 is ~3%. Higher-order interpolation (5-point, duo-grid) gives diminishing returns for the same reason.

./docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-251-1. **Accept O(dx) artifacts**: At C48+, artifacts are < 0.4 m/s and may be acceptable for coupled ESM. The baseline model at C36 shows L2=0.013 (5-day TC2, stable), max|v|=1.4 m/s, mass drift < 1e-7. This is competitive with published cubed-sphere solvers.

./docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-253-2. **Higher-order halo exchange** (DONE, iteration 9): Upgraded pad_halo halo=1 from 2-point linear to 3-point quadratic Lagrange. Provides ~3% reduction in max |v| edge artifacts. Limited improvement because for smooth geostrophic fields, B''' ≈ B''/h, so the O(h³→h²) gradient error improvement is only O(h) ≈ 1/36 at C36. Further upgrades (5-point, duo-grid) would give diminishing returns for the same reason.

./docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-255-3. **Switch to FV3's normal D-grid layout** (GFDL convention): Each velocity component at its NORMAL face (u_ξ at ξ-face, u_η at η-face). This enables simple 2-point gradients WITHOUT the Cartesian matrix — eliminating the error source entirely. Requires rewriting ALL cubed-sphere operators, mass transport, halo exchange, and initial conditions. Multi-month effort.

./docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-261-**Finding**: The halo=1 scalar exchange path used only **2-point LINEAR interpolation** (O(dx²) error, O(dx) gradient error), while the halo=2 path already used 3-point quadratic Lagrange (O(dx³), O(dx²) gradient). This was the smoking gun — the halo=1 path is used by ALL cubed-sphere operators including the A-L gradient.

./docs/dev-notes/cubed_sphere_edge_artifacts.md-275-**Why only ~3% improvement**: For a smooth geostrophic field (TC2), B''' ≈ B''/h. This means the O(h³→h²) gradient error improvement from quadratic→cubic is only O(h) ≈ 1/n, which at C36 is ~3%. Higher-order interpolation (5-point, duo-grid) gives diminishing returns for the same reason.

./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-1-#!/bin/bash
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-2-#SBATCH --account=glab
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-3-#SBATCH --partition=glab1
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-4-#SBATCH --job-name=trpsbc_ab
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-5-#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-6-#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-7-#SBATCH --mem=96G
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-8-#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-9-#SBATCH --output=/burg-archive/glab/users/pg2328/legoESM/omip_nemo/trpsbc_ab_%j.out
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-10-# A/B: NEMO Dirichlet vs Veros-flux surface-TKE BC on the tripole zdftke path.
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-11-# CONTROLLED: identical trp5 ship command, SAME tree (main, /burg), d30; the
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-12-# ONLY variable is --tke-surface-bc ($SBC).  Hypothesis: the summer-hemisphere
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch:13:# surface-intensified warm (SST +0.53, SHmid +1.07 / antarctic +0.97 / tropics
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-14-# +0.71 at d30 vs NEMO; profile probe = ML heat wedge) is under-mixed by the
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-15-# Veros flux (|tau|/rho0)^{3/2} BC; NEMO's linear Dirichlet en(1)=rn_ebb|tau|/
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-16-# rho0 injects more surface TKE under moderate summer winds -> cools the ML.
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-17-# Compare the two arms at d30 (NEMO month=1, seasonally matched to a Jan d30).
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-18-set +e
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-19-: "${SBC:?set SBC=veros_flux|nemo_dirichlet via --export}"
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-20-ROOT=/burg/glab/users/pg2328/legoESM; cd $ROOT
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-21-export PYTHONPATH="$(ls -d $ROOT/packages/*/ | sed 's:/$::' | tr '\n' ':')$ROOT:$ROOT/scripts/validate"
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-22-PY=/burg-archive/glab/users/jn2808/.conda/envs/legoesm/bin/python
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-23-N=/burg-archive/glab/users/pg2328/nemo_orca1/nemo_5.0.1
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-24-RUN=$N/cfgs/ORCA1/EXP00/RUN_REF; INP=$N/cfgs/ORCA1/INPUTS/orca1_inputs/data_repository/input_fields
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-25-INITD=$N/cfgs/ORCA1/INPUTS/orca1_inputs/data_repository/initial_conditions
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-26-GT=$RUN/ORCA1_1m_20000101_20041231_grid_T.nc
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-27-WTIC=$ROOT/data/woce_gouretski/woce_t_woa57_annual.nc
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-28-WSIC=$ROOT/data/woce_gouretski/woce_s_woa57_annual.nc
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-29-SSSCLIM=$INP/sss_climatology_for_restoring.nc
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-30-ICEIC=$N/cfgs/ORCA1/INPUTS/Ice_initialization.nc
./scripts/cluster/omip_nemo/_ab_tke_surface_bc.sbatch-31-echo "=== HOST ==="; hostname; nvidia-smi -L 2>/dev/null | head -1; date

r512 (512x1024 = 524k cols) L26 f64 moist, 32 rpn block:cyclic,
wall-pole 2-D pencil lane (labelled; NOT the pole fold):

| ranks | cols/rank | ms/step | speedup vs np64 | eff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 8,192 | 297.57 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| 128 | 4,096 | 161.03 | 1.848 | 0.92 |
| 256 | 2,048 | 72.06 | 4.129 | 1.03 |

Distribution verified against the masquerade trap: result rows carry
`n_ranks: 512` (the JSON's `metadata.process_count: 1` is the jax-LOCAL
count on this mpi4jax lane, not the world size). 128->256 is
SUPERLINEAR (2.23x for 2x) — classic per-rank working-set cache
transition on Milan (mechanism PLAUSIBLE, uninstrumented). End-to-end
64->512 eff 0.83 at 1k cols/rank: TIMING-ONLY evidence that the lat-lon
CPU lane scales into the hundreds. QUALIFIER (codex r22): the run logs
an out-of-tested-range mpi4jax==0.9.0 pairing ("may fail or produce
incorrect results", parallel/reductions.py runtime check) and UCX
VM_UNMAP warnings — no parity/conservation gate ran, so this ladder is
unvalidated timing evidence until a supported-stack rerun. (Exact pencil factorisations are not recorded in the
result JSON — only `decomposition: 2d`; a follow-up could add them to
the bench metadata.)

s8 np8/16/32, lloyd=0, f32, sfc + `--reorder-for 128`, steps 12 /
warmup 3 — configuration-matched to the s9 ladder (26600095); NOT fully
reproduction-grade: the s9 np32 row's git_sha reads `unknown`, and this
run's `7151d12a1-dirty` has no archived dirty-file manifest (the live
diff touched only doc+plot, which supports but cannot retrospectively
prove the bench path was untouched): **6.58 / 6.43 / 7.29 ms**.

Weak pairs (~4x cells with 4x GPUs — global ratio 3.9994 after both
meshes pad +126 cells; tiles NEAR-matched to 0.015 %:
81,936/81,924, 40,968/40,962, 20,484/20,481), SAME lloyd-0 family:

| cells/GPU | s8 rung | s9 rung | ratio | weak eff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 81.9k | np8 6.58 | np32 12.47 | 1.895 | **0.53** |
| 41.0k | np16 6.43 | np64 9.60 | 1.493 | 0.67 |
| 20.5k | np32 7.29 | np128 11.48 | 1.575 | 0.64 |

* The falsifiability block's CONFIRM branch fires: ratios stay well
  above 1 with the known Lloyd-family mismatch REMOVED. (This does not
  prove the old confound "only" biased the size — these are
  unreplicated single runs from separate allocations, one comparator
  without row-level provenance; the confounded draft read
  1.80/1.35/1.41 vs 1.90/1.49/1.57 here, and the production-mesh s8
  np8 was 6.92 vs lloyd-0 6.58, -4.9 %, so the mesh family does shift
  absolutes.)
* Restated: at NEAR-matched per-GPU tile, ~quadrupling devices+problem
  costs 1.5-1.9x on this lane — the GPU-side analogue of the ocean CPU
  scale-out term. Weak efficiency 0.53-0.67 at 4x. Mechanism still
  UNATTRIBUTED (PLAUSIBLE candidates unchanged: inter-node neighbour
  fraction growth, collective latency vs count, sfc partition-quality
  decay with parts; the metis receipt argues against pure
  partition-cut explanations, on the CPU lane at least).
* The non-monotone tile dependence of the ratio (largest at the
  LARGEST tile, 1.90 at 81.9k) is unexplained; recorded, not theorised.
